changelog: - **A mark stays where a revision left phase names and timing on different sides.** Before an Apply that takes a proposal’s phase names without its timetables or step length, or its timing without its names, the review already said that the current phase shown may then differ from the real process. That notice was gone once the review closed. Now the document keeps it: the run row shows a small mark beside the phase name, on the desktop row and on the phone line, and its press opens the sentence. A screen reader hears it with the phase, once. The mark says the names may not match, not that they do not. It goes away when you undo that Apply, when a later Apply takes phase names and timing together from a proposal that has no mark, when the phases are removed, or when you press “I checked the phases and the timetables”, which records your own check and can itself be undone. That button is on the desktop, and not while the edit lock is on. The mark is part of the document: it is saved with a file, comes back after a reload, travels in a project revision or a proposal, and the review’s “Run phases” line says when taking a proposal’s phases brings it or takes it off. Project revision files declare `loop-revision/15`. An earlier version of the app opens a marked document without the mark and saves it without it, and it reports a marked project revision as written by a newer version; a document with no mark is unchanged byte for byte.
